nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a Boolean equality test, not necessarily lawful, and let $s$ be a word of length $n$ over $\alpha$. For every position $i < n$, the entry at $i$ of the Z-array computed by the Z-algorithm on $s$ is at most $n - i$.
nodes.title: Z-values are at most the suffix length

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a lawful Boolean equality test, let $s = s_0 \dots s_{n-1}$ be a word over $\alpha$, and let $Z$ be the Z-array computed by the Z-algorithm on $s$. For every position $i < n$ and every natural number $q$, $q \le Z_i$ holds if and only if $q \le n - i$ and $s_k = s_{i+k}$ for all $k < q$. Hence $Z_i$ is the length of the longest common prefix of $s$ and its suffix $s_i \dots s_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Z-values are longest common prefix lengths

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a lawful Boolean equality test and let $a \ne b$ be elements of $\alpha$. For every $n \ge 1$, the Z-algorithm run on the word $a^n b$ has cost exactly $3n - 1$, where the cost counts one unit for each visited position $i \ge 1$ and one unit for each symbol comparison. In terms of the input length $N = n + 1$, this is $3N - 4$.
nodes.title: Z-algorithm cost on a repeated symbol followed by a distinct one

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a lawful Boolean equality test, let $a \in \alpha$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The Z-algorithm run on the word $a^n$ has cost exactly $2(n - 1)$, read as $0$ when $n = 0$, where the cost counts one unit for each visited position $i \ge 1$ and one unit for each symbol comparison. Thus it makes $n - 1$ visits and $n - 1$ comparisons.
nodes.title: Z-algorithm cost on a repeated symbol

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a lawful Boolean equality test, let $a \in \alpha$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The Z-array computed by the Z-algorithm on the word $a^n$ has entry $n - i$ at every position $i < n$.
nodes.title: Z-array of a repeated symbol

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a Boolean equality test, not necessarily lawful. On every word of length $n$ over $\alpha$, the Z-algorithm has cost at least $n - 1$, where the cost counts one unit for each visited position $i \ge 1$ and one unit for each symbol comparison.
nodes.title: Linear lower bound for the Z-algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a Boolean equality test, not necessarily lawful. On every word of length $n$ over $\alpha$, the Z-algorithm has cost at most $3(n - 1)$, read as $0$ when $n = 0$, where the cost counts one unit for each visited position $i \ge 1$ and one unit for each symbol comparison.
nodes.title: Linear upper bound for the Z-algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a Boolean equality test. For every nonempty word of length $n$ over $\alpha$, the Z-array $Z$ computed by the Z-algorithm has $Z_0 = n$.
nodes.title: The first Z-value is the word length

nodes.summary: Given a word $s = s_0 \dots s_{n-1}$ over a type $\alpha$ with a Boolean equality test, Gusfield's Z-box algorithm returns an array $Z$ of $n$ natural numbers with $Z_0 = n$. It visits $i = 1, \dots, n - 1$ in turn, keeping a box $[\ell, r)$, initially empty, that is the rightmost match of a prefix of $s$ found so far. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
